intro: «Como si» compares with something unreal and always takes a past subjunctive, whatever the tense of the main verb.
p.como si.consejo: It asks for the imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive: «como si fuera», «como si hubiera visto».
p.ni que.glosa: as if; it is not as though
p.ni que.consejo: It is colloquial and takes the past subjunctive: «¡ni que fuera gratis!». It is used to play something down.
p.como si nada.consejo: It is a set phrase: «siguió trabajando como si nada». It never changes.
p.parece que.consejo: When you affirm, it takes the indicative: «parece que va a llover». It does not take the subjunctive.
p.hacer como que.consejo: It means to pretend and takes the indicative: «hace como que no me ve».
p.fingir.consejo: The g sounds like h before i: fin-HIR. With «que» it takes the indicative: «finge que duerme».
p.tratar.consejo: With a person, «me trata bien» speaks of how he behaves. With «de» it means to try: «trato de ayudar».
p.fantasma.consejo: It is masculine although it ends in -a: «el fantasma». The stress falls on «tas».
p.el nuevo.consejo: Here «nuevo» works as a noun. If it is a woman, you say «la nueva».
p.toda la vida.consejo: It is an exaggeration: it means «since forever» or «for very many years».
b1.texto:
**Como si** compares with something that is not true. The verb that follows goes in the **past subjunctive**:

- Habla **como si fuera** el jefe. (he is not)
- Me mira **como si estuviera** loco. (he is not)

If the comparison looks at something earlier, use **hubiera** + participle:

- Estás pálido, **como si hubieras visto** un fantasma.

The main verb can be in any tense: habla, hablaba, habló **como si fuera** el dueño.
b2.f0.texto: The new guy talks as if he were the boss.
b2.f1.texto: Yes, he treats us as if we knew nothing.
b2.f2.texto: Yesterday he looked at me as if he had seen a ghost.
b2.f3.texto: Then he carried on working as if nothing had happened.
b2.f4.texto: As if he had been here all his life!
b2.f5.texto: It seems he does not realise.
b2.f6.texto: He is surely pretending not to hear us.
b2.f7.texto: Tomorrow we greet him as if nothing had happened.
b4.texto:
**Como si** + **imperfect subjunctive** compares with something unreal happening at the same time: habla como si lo **supiera**.

**Como si** + **hubiera** + participle compares with something unreal that came before: como si **hubiera visto** un fantasma.

It never takes the present subjunctive or the indicative.

In colloquial language: **¡Ni que** + imperfect subjunctive**!** ¡Ni que fuera gratis!

Two similar expressions take the **indicative**:

- **Parece que** va a llover.
- **Hace como que** no me ve. Finge que no me ve.
b4.e0.texto: He talks as if he were the owner.
b4.e1.texto: He is pale, as if he had seen a ghost.
b4.e2.texto: He pretends he does not see me.
b5.f0.texto: The new colleague crosses the office with long, confident steps.
b5.f1.texto: He walks as if the floor were his.
b5.f2.texto: His perfume leaves a trail of wood and lemon in the corridor.
b5.f3.texto: The others raise their eyes from their screens and follow him with their gaze.
b5.f4.texto: In the silence, the air turns thick like a stormy afternoon.
b5.f5.texto: Yesterday, on seeing him by the window, Lucía felt a shiver.
b5.f6.texto: The new man looked at her for a second, without smiling and without speaking.
b5.f7.texto: Then he carried on typing as if nothing had happened.
b5.f8.texto: The computer keys sounded like little drops on a roof.
b5.f9.texto: Little by little, the office went back to breathing normally.
b6.o0: Habla como si es el jefe.
b6.o0.refuerzo: «Es» is indicative and «como si» does not accept it here.
b6.o1: Habla como si fuera el jefe.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Yes! «Como si» asks for the imperfect subjunctive.
b6.o2: Habla como si sea el jefe.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Sea» is present subjunctive: «como si» does not use it.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Correct: something unreal and simultaneous asks for the imperfect subjunctive.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Está» states that it is true; «como si» compares with the unreal.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Esté» is present subjunctive and is not used with «como si».
b7.pregunta: He is not mad, but he looks it.
b8.frase: Habla como si fuera el jefe
b8.traduccion: He talks as if he were the boss
b9.frase: Estás pálido, como si ____ un fantasma.
b9.o0.refuerzo: «Has visto» is indicative; «como si» asks for the subjunctive.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Habrías visto» is conditional; it does not follow «como si».
b9.o2.refuerzo: That's it! «Hubieras visto» expresses something unreal and earlier.
b9.pregunta: It looks as if you saw something earlier. Which form is missing?
b10.o0: Parece que no se da cuenta.
b10.o0.refuerzo: Correct: affirmative «parece que» takes the indicative.
b10.o1: Parece que no se dé cuenta.
b10.o1.refuerzo: «Dé» is subjunctive; it is not needed here.
b10.o2: Parece que no se diera cuenta.
b10.o2.refuerzo: «Diera» is past subjunctive and does not fit either.
b10.pregunta: Which sentence with «parece que» is correct?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «He talks as if he were the boss.»
b12.o0.refuerzo: On the contrary: «ni que» rejects that idea.
b12.o1.refuerzo: Well done! The speaker criticises someone who acts as if it were free.
b12.o2.refuerzo: The sentence makes it clear that it is not.
b12.pregunta: «¡Ni que fuera gratis!» Is it free?
p.trata.consejo: From «tratar». The r after t is a soft tap: TRA-ta.
p.miró.consejo: Past tense of «mirar», he or she. The accent marks the last syllable.
p.siguió.consejo: Past tense of «seguir». The «gu» before i is the sound g, as in «gato»; the stress is at the end.
p.llevara.consejo: The imperfect subjunctive of «llevar». Here it means «had been here».
p.saludamos.consejo: From «saludar», to greet: the «-amos» ending is for nosotros.
p.finge.consejo: From «fingir». The g before e sounds like a soft h in Spain: FIN-je.
p.cruza.consejo: From «cruzar». The z sounds like th in Spain.
p.pasos.consejo: Plural of «paso». The -s is a soft hiss at the end.
p.seguros.consejo: Plural of «seguro», it describes the steps: «pasos seguros».
p.estela.consejo: It is the trail left behind by something that passes.
p.vista.consejo: In «levantar la vista» it means looking up. The v sounds like b.
p.pantallas.consejo: Plural of «pantalla». The ll sounds like y.
p.siguen.consejo: From «seguir». The gu before e sounds like g.
p.mirada.consejo: From «mirar». It describes how someone looks.
p.espeso.consejo: Espeso se usa for air or liquids that feel heavy: «aire espeso».
p.sintió.consejo: Past tense of «sentir», he or she. The accent is at the end.
p.escalofrío.consejo: The accent makes FRI the stressed syllable.
p.segundo.consejo: It is also the ordinal «second»; here it is the unit of time.
p.sonreír.consejo: The infinitive. The accent on the í marks the stress at the end.
p.escribiendo.consejo: The gerund of «escribir». It means «while writing».
p.ordenador.consejo: In Spain «ordenador» is the computer; in Latin America it is «computadora».
p.sonaban.consejo: Past tense of «sonar», they. The stress is on NA.
p.volvió.consejo: Past tense of «volver», he or she. The accent is at the end: bol-BIO.
p.normalidad.consejo: It ends in -dad, a common ending for nouns that name a quality.
p.loco.consejo: In «como si ____ loco» the verb after «si» takes the imperfect subjunctive.
p.gratis.consejo: It is the same in both forms: «gratis» is said as GRA-tis.
p.supiéramos.consejo: The imperfect subjunctive of «saber» with «nosotros». It takes an accent on «ra».
